QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_23

question.text: Hariyali Foundation runs a water-purification programme under SAS-200 providing safe drinking water. A critical ETHICAL materiality question is whether the SIA should disclose:

answer.text: The brand name of the filter installed
A failure in 18% of filter units found during physical inspection, even though the SE reports 'all units functional'

explanation.text: **The Logic:** An 18% failure rate observed by independent SIA inspection is material, contradicts SE's 'all functional' claim, and MUST be disclosed — it goes to the honesty of the Report. Option B individual-names is PII and should be anonymised. Option A brand and Option D donor-split are not material to the impact conclusion. **The Trap:** Options A, B, D are distractors — they are about details that are either non-material or PII. **Cross-Exam Context:** Exception-reporting and materiality judgement also figure in III-A / III-C (Compliance — whistleblower and exception escalation). **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** Never delete negative findings from the draft report under SE pressure — the firm's SRO Registration Number (on the report signature block) is what peer-review checks back against.
